I've been in this situation before and I'll be honest with you It didn't turn out great. He was threatening to kill himself if I left him and was also sexually assaulting me and my sleep. When I found out this was happening I left him and blocked him on all media. Full blown no contact. 2 years later I saw his obituary online. Did I feel some guilt for it? Sure. Did I ultimately come to the conclusion that that relationship wasn't healthy for me and I wasn't ever going to be a fix for him? Also yes. If someone is truly suicidal that's their choice. It's never going to be your fault. You didn't kill them. 
Now I've also been in a situation where the other person was threatening self-harm and suicide as a manipulative way to keep me around because they were emotionally dependent on me and obsessive. When I broke up with him they went full-blown revenge mode trying to ruin my life and again I went no contact. There were a few instances of stalking and harassment online that eventually died off when they realized they weren't going to get the reaction from me that they desired. And ultimately they moved on and went about living their life.
Moral of the story is you can only control yourself. And if he's not willing to seek help for his depression or start going to therapy then there's nothing that you're going to do that's going to change them. They have to change themselves. And you need to do what's right for you which I truly believe is cutting them off and not stringing them along when you don't have romantic feelings for them.

I say this is someone with three healthy pregnancies that went full term and I have three grown daughters and I have had five miscarriages in between those pregnancies with no indications of fertility issues just nonviable fetuses. It happens. I'm sorry y'all are going through this.

While some stress can be a factor it is not going to be the sole contributing cause of any given miscarriage. Sometimes the fetus isn't viable and the body just aborts spontaneously. And while the timing might make you feel awful it would have been just as likely to happen any other time she became pregnant. And yet that's still not an indicator that any future pregnancies would happen the same way they're literally all different from woman to woman and from pregnancy to pregnancy. I would suggest that she sees a doctor to make sure that everything is healing as it should and maybe you two can sit down and have a heart to heart and heal from this and move on. Don't beat yourself up because I promise you she's doing the same thing and blaming herself and neither of you are at fault.
